definition: Microsoft Voice Command is an application which can control Windows Mobile devices by voice.
details: The first version was announced in November 2003 and it was supported in the United Kingdom, United States, France, and Germany. Windows Mobile 6.5 had Microsoft TellMe integration, software created by a company Microsoft had recently acquired. This feature was later implemented in Windows Phone as a part of Bing Mobile.

explainer.lead: Microsoft Voice Command is an application that controls Windows Mobile devices by voice. It matters as an early step toward voice control on mobile devices.

tiers.eli5: It let you talk to your phone to make it do things, back when phones were running Windows Mobile.

tiers.paperLevel: An application for voice control of Windows Mobile devices; version one was announced November 2003 with support in the UK, US, France, and Germany.

explainer.example: A Windows Mobile user issues a spoken command and the application acts on it.
